body:
**Problem**

With `laststatus=3`, the row between two stacked windows is a horizontal separator (`w_hsep_height == 1`), not a statusline — but a click on it is handled as a global-statusline click.

**Steps to reproduce**

```vim
nvim --clean
:set laststatus=3
:lua _G.Hit = function() print("HIT") end
:set statusline=%7@v:lua.Hit@CLICKME%T
:split
```

On the separator between the two windows (not the bottom row of the screen):

1. click `CLICKME` → `HIT` is printed, although the click is not on a statusline;
2. press `CLICKME` and drag up/down → the split does not resize;
3. drag from a blank column of the same separator → the split resizes (control, so the drag itself works).

**Actual**

The statusline click handler under the cursor runs, and the divider drag is swallowed.

**Expected**

The separator only resizes the split; statusline click regions are live only on the real global statusline.

**Analysis**

With `laststatus=3` a non-last window has `w_status_height == 0` / `w_hsep_height == 1`. `jump_to_mouse()` (`src/nvim/mouse.c`) sets `IN_STATUS_LINE` for that frame row because it only tests whether the row is at/below the window text area (`below_window`); `get_fpos_of_mouse()` has the additional check that it must be the global statusline row:

```c
mouse_row >= Rows - p_ch - global_stl_height()
```

`do_mouse()` then takes the global-statusline path and dispatches `curwin->w_status_click_defs` by absolute screen column (`call_click_def_func()`), so the component under the cursor fires. That call also resets `got_click`, which is why the drag no longer resizes.

**Version**

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1824+g27ee55c09d, Windows 11 / Windows Terminal. Reproduces with no plugins or config (`-u NONE`), with `cmdheight=0` and `cmdheight=1`; the affected code is core mouse handling, so it is not platform-specific.

**Scripted check**

<details><summary>repro.lua (deterministic, 80x24 embedded UI)</summary>

```lua
-- Repro: with 'laststatus' = 3, a click on the horizontal separator between two
-- stacked windows runs the statusline click handler, and dragging that
-- separator does not resize the windows.
--
-- Run: nvim --headless -u NONE -c "luafile repro.lua" -c "qa!"
-- (uses a nested nvim --embed with a 80x24 UI; no plugins, no config)
local exe = vim.v.progpath
local chan = vim.fn.jobstart({ exe, "--embed", "-u", "NONE" }, { rpc = true })
local function req(...)
    return vim.fn.rpcrequest(chan, ...)
end
local function lua(code)
    return req("nvim_exec_lua", code, {})
end

req("nvim_ui_attach", 80, 24, {})
lua([[
  vim.o.laststatus = 3
  vim.o.mouse = 'a'
  _G.hits = 0
  _G.Hit = function() _G.hits = _G.hits + 1 end
  vim.o.statusline = '%7@v:lua.Hit@CLICKME%T'
  vim.cmd('split')
  vim.cmd('redraw!')
  vim.cmd('redrawstatus!')
]])
vim.wait(300, function()
    return false
end)

local wins = lua([[
  local r = {}
  for _, w in ipairs(vim.api.nvim_list_wins()) do
    local p = vim.api.nvim_win_get_position(w)
    r[#r + 1] = { id = w, row = p[1], height = vim.api.nvim_win_get_height(w) }
  end
  return r
]])
local top = wins[1]
for _, w in ipairs(wins) do
    if w.row < top.row then
        top = w
    end
end
local hsep = top.row + top.height -- 0-based screen row of the separator
local gstl = lua("return vim.o.lines - 1 - vim.o.cmdheight")

local function press(row, col)
    req("nvim_input_mouse", "left", "press", "", 0, row, col)
    vim.wait(200, function()
        return false
    end)
end
local function release(row, col)
    req("nvim_input_mouse", "left", "release", "", 0, row, col)
    vim.wait(100, function()
        return false
    end)
end
local function height()
    return lua("return vim.api.nvim_win_get_height(" .. top.id .. ")")
end

print(("top row=%d height=%d -> hsep row %d, global statusline row %d"):format(top.row, top.height, hsep, gstl))
local h = lua("return _G.hits")
press(hsep, 3)
release(hsep, 3)
print("click hsep, clickable column: handler ran = " .. tostring(lua("return _G.hits") ~= h) .. "   (expected false)")

local before = height()
press(hsep, 3)
req("nvim_input_mouse", "left", "drag", "", 0, hsep - 3, 3)
vim.wait(200, function()
    return false
end)
req("nvim_input_mouse", "left", "release", "", 0, hsep - 3, 3)
vim.wait(200, function()
    return false
end)
print(("drag hsep, clickable column:  height %d -> %d   (expected change)"):format(before, height()))

before = height()
press(hsep, 60) -- blank part of the separator, outside any click region
req("nvim_input_mouse", "left", "drag", "", 0, hsep - 3, 60)
vim.wait(200, function()
    return false
end)
req("nvim_input_mouse", "left", "release", "", 0, hsep - 3, 60)
vim.wait(200, function()
    return false
end)
print(("drag hsep, blank column:      height %d -> %d   (control, expected change)"):format(before, height()))

local h2 = lua("return _G.hits")
press(gstl, 3)
print("click global statusline:      handler ran = " .. tostring(lua("return _G.hits") ~= h2) .. "   (expected true)")
release(gstl, 3)

vim.fn.jobstop(chan)
```

Output:

```
top row=0 height=11 -> hsep row 11, global statusline row 22
click hsep, clickable column: handler ran = true   (expected false)
drag hsep, clickable column:  height 11 -> 11   (expected change)
drag hsep, blank column:      height 11 -> 8   (control, expected change)
click global statusline:      handler ran = true   (expected true)
```

</details>

**Possible fix**

In `do_mouse()`, require the mouse row to be the global statusline row before dispatching click defs (the same condition `get_fpos_of_mouse()` uses), or keep `w_hsep_height` rows out of the statusline click path.
title: mouse: click on a split's horizontal separator runs statusline click handlers and blocks the resize drag
